findings.passage: Before, non-citizen voting was just a hypothetical, but now we know it’s really happening – and we’ll never know how often. This event proved that voter ID laws are long overdue.
findings.note: Statement in her name, issued when she became chair of the House election committee, linking a reported case of a non-citizen voting to the case for voter ID laws.

findings.passage: Proof of citizenship should absolutely be required to vote in our elections, and I am sure the vast majority of my fellow election clerks would agree. Secretary Benson and her team should complete a thorough review of our voter rolls and ensure that only living U.S. citizens, who reside in Michigan, are able to validly cast a vote at the polls in the future.
findings.note: She says proof of citizenship should be required to vote and calls for a review of the voter rolls. Quoted in a House caucus release; the same quote also appears at https://www.michigannewssource.com/?p=60995 (2025-04-07).

findings.passage: My husband and I had to prove our citizenship when we adopted our children. Never once, in any of these life experiences, did I feel disenfranchised.
findings.note: Argues from personal experience that showing citizenship documents is not a burden, in support of House Joint Resolution B (proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote).

findings.passage: I was glad to attend the hearing to support Rep. Bollin’s testimony on the MEGA Act. I hope to help craft and introduce similar legislation at the state level so we can continue working closely with our federal partners on election security.
findings.note: She backs a federal bill that sets voter ID, citizenship verification for registration and voter-list upkeep (as described on the same page) and says she wants similar state legislation; the page also says she joined in presenting a state House resolution backing the SAVE Act.

findings.passage: “I think we need answers on that. How was he on the rolls, how was he not removed?”
findings.note: Quoted by Michigan Public at a Lansing press conference about a video alleging a non-citizen on the voter rolls; the same event backed a voter ID ballot amendment. The outlet quoted her; the page is not her own site.

findings.passage: The charges filed today are just the tip of the iceberg, and further underscore exactly why the U.S. Senate must approve the SAVE Act to safeguard our elections and ensure only U.S. citizens are voting in our elections.
findings.note: Statement in her name after state charges against five non-citizens; she calls on the U.S. Senate to pass the SAVE Act, which the release describes as requiring proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote.

findings.passage: Now that I am serving as Chair during this legislative term, my focus is to bring about good policies and laws that can be quickly passed to clean up our voter file, kick out illegal ballots from elections, and properly investigate serious and credible evidence of systemic voter fraud in our Michigan elections.
findings.note: Issue page on her official site (date taken from the page's own publish data) stating her goals as committee chair, including voter-file cleanup; the page also lists her election bills and press releases.

findings.passage: “I absolutely think that it was stolen, yeah, and I’m not shy to say that,”
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat from an interview, about the 2020 presidential election; saved as related election-integrity talk, not as a statement on ID. The outlet quoted her.
